subject: Post-call: Shopline rerank proof plan & benchmarks
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Shopline rerank proof plan & benchmarks
Attachments: shopline_rerank_benchmark_v1.csv; prompt_set_shopline_v2.txt; mutual_action_plan.docx

Hi Jenny / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the recommended path to validate a reranking model for search relevance:

What we heard
- Primary objective: lift relevance for category & query intent mixes where current TF-IDF+BM25 blend underperforms (notably: promotion-driven queries, short tail branded queries).
- Constraints: 99th‑percentile latency targets of <= 120ms for search API, per-request cost sensitivity.
- Success metrics: NDCG@10, MRR, and downstream CTR / add-to-cart for the top 3 results.

Redwood’s recommended PoC configuration
- Candidate reranker: llama3-13b-rerank (8-bit quantized) as a cross-encoder reranker for top-50 hits.
- Lightweight candidate encoder for recall: small bi-encoder (open-sparse-2) at recall stage.
- Canary size: 5% of live search queries for 2 weeks (min 250k queries) or until statistical significance on NDCG/MRR.
- Safety nets: prefix caching for repeated queries, automatic fallback to current ranking if 95th-percentile latency > 140ms or error rate > 0.2%.

Initial benchmark highlights (attached CSV) — base vs candidate rerank on held-out Shopline sample set:
- Baseline (current ranker): NDCG@10 = 0.62, MRR = 0.41
- Candidate reranker (llama3-13b-rerank): NDCG@10 = 0.73, MRR = 0.53
- Delta: +0.11 NDCG@10, +0.12 MRR (relative uplift ~18–29% depending on slice)

Quality/regression concerns we flagged
- Promotions/price tokens: model sometimes over-prioritizes items with promo text present in description; will add targeted prompt tests and demotion rules.
- Synonym brittleness on short branded queries — we have a prompt-set that stresses these cases (attached prompt_set_shopline_v2.txt).

Next steps / asks from Shopline
1) Confirm a kickoff window for a 5% live canary (preferably next week).
2) Provide a point of contact for procurement/PO so we can align on billing for reserved inference capacity during the PoC.
3) Share any additional priority query slices (promo-heavy categories, homepage search) to include in the initial measure set.

I’ve attached the benchmark CSV and the prompt set we’ll use for regression monitoring, plus a one-page mutual action plan doc for signatures. If this matches your expectations I’ll schedule the kickoff and loop in Engineering for a short runbook review.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0126
